results.title: Why do I get an error in Typescript when I use a generic as a return value? - Stack Overflow
results.snippet: I don't know why the error is reported. Can anyone help me? ... The problem stems from the fact that your function claims it will return an object of type T, but in fact you could be returning a type that's narrower (a subtype) of T.

results.title: Typescript Function with Generic Return Type - Stack Overflow
results.snippet: The type ... is a concrete type referring to a generic function. <T>() => T means: "a function whose caller specifies a type T and which returns a value of type T." This is essentially impossible to implement safely.

results.title: TypeScript: Documentation - Generics
results.snippet: While using any is certainly generic in that it will cause the function to accept any and all types for the type of arg, we actually are losing the information about what that type was when the function returns.
